title: End-to-end Generate→Verify→Repair (GVR) for Intent-to-Configuration Safety — Repaired Preregistration
research_question: Does an end-to-end generate→verify→repair pipeline that integrates an LLM, a deterministic network verifier, and a network emulator materially reduce operational-safety violations in LLM-generated network configurations compared to LLM-only generation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: A GVR pipeline reduces the proportion of intents producing at least one safety-policy violation (verifier flag + emulator-confirmed) by ≥30 percentage points relative to LLM-only generation (paired within-intent comparison).
H2: Repairs produced by the GVR pipeline do not increase median emulator-observed configuration latency by more than 10% relative to the original LLM outputs (paired within-intent comparison).
exploratory_questions: E1: How many repair iterations are typically required per violated intent (distribution of repair iterations)?
E2: Which verifier-flag classes (reachability, ACL, loop/policy) are most amenable to automatic repair?
E3: Vendor-conditional effects: does GVR effectiveness vary by vendor CLI family (Cisco, Juniper, Arista)?
benchmark_scope: Publicly collectible NetOps natural-language intents (snapshot URIs published at time of run).
Emulator-only execution (Mininet-based topologies in Docker containers).
Deterministic, rule-based verifier coverage limited to reachability, ACL/ACL-order, loop/forwarding-loop, and explicit policy contradictions as encoded in the verifier ruleset.
primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in proportions of intents that produce at least one safety-policy violation (verifier flag that is confirmed as emulator-failure) between LLM-only and GVR-final configurations.
secondary_estimands: Paired median difference in emulator-observed TCP/ICMP latency proxy between LLM-only and GVR-final configs per intent.
Distribution of repair iterations per intent (mean, median, IQR).
Per-violation-type (reachability, ACL, loop/policy) absolute reduction in violation proportion.
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample N=100 unique natural-language NetOps intents. Stratified by vendor-family: Cisco=34, Juniper=33, Arista=33. Intent sourcing automated via deterministic crawlers of public instructional pages, open-source labs, vendor examples, and community problem lists; filter heuristics require concrete connectivity or policy objective. Final sampled set is snapshot (URI list + hash) and published. Inclusion: English actionable intent with reachable topology mapping. Exclusion: intents requiring proprietary devices or private data.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand target: absolute reduction ≥30 percentage points (e.g., from 40% to 10%). Paired McNemar test (two-sided, alpha=0.05) for H1; 10k bootstrap percentile CIs for paired proportion differences. Power approximation: with N=100 and assumed baseline p1=0.40, p2=0.10, estimated power ≈0.85. Sensitivity analyses for baseline rates {0.25,0.35,0.45}. For latency (H2) use paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (two-sided, alpha=0.05) and bootstrap CIs for median ratio.
exclusion_rules: Intents requiring proprietary hardware, private data, or nondeterministic external dependencies.
Items for which all execution artifacts remain unavailable after automated retries (treated per missingness_plan).
missingness_plan: Automated retry policy for infrastructure faults: up to 2 automated re-executions (same seed/config). If still unavailable, the intent is excluded from confirmatory paired analysis and recorded in a missingness table. Sensitivity analyses: complete-case and worst-case imputations (two pre-registered worst-case assignments). All exclusions and deterministic failure reasons published.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison of per-intent binary outcome (safety violation yes/no) between LLM-only and GVR-final configs. Use exact McNemar test (two-sided, alpha=0.05); report discordant-pair table, absolute and relative reductions, and 95% bootstrap percentile CIs (10k resamples). For latency (H2), compute paired differences in per-intent median latency proxies and test with Wilcoxon signed-rank (two-sided); report median ratio and bootstrap 95% CI. Pre-registered subgroup (vendor) analyses with Bonferroni correction. Publish all raw counts and per-intent artifacts. Analysis code deterministic and published (Docker + seed).
multiplicity_plan: Primary familywise alpha reserved for H1 only. Per-vendor subgroup tests (3) use Bonferroni correction (alpha_adj=0.05/3). All other secondary analyses reported with nominal p-values and labeled exploratory.
contamination_plan: Publish all prompt texts and LLM responses. Automated substring checks will flag potential leakage: an intent is 'potentially contaminated' if any LLM response contains a >80-character verbatim span matching any source URI content in the intent corpus snapshot. Flag repeated identical outputs across seeds/templates as 'duplicate-output'. Primary analyses exclude flagged contaminated items; secondary analyses include them with labels. All flagged items published with redaction as required.
stopping_rule: Stop when all N=100 intents have completed baseline and guarded episodes (including allowed retries) or when deterministic infrastructure cutoff is reached. If more than 10% of intents are unrecoverably missing after retries, stop and report outcomes with missingness sensitivity analyses; do not continue adaptive sampling beyond the pre-registered N.
planned_outputs: All prompt templates, seeds, and raw LLM responses.
Parsed vendor-CLI ASTs, verifier JSON reports, emulator logs, and per-intent test results.
Analysis code and Docker image for replication.
Statistical results: McNemar tables, effect sizes, bootstrap CIs, latency tests.
Five-page IEEE-format manuscript with Disclosure Statement.
